Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 64, verses 7–13:

His saying: ﴿The disbelievers claim that they will never be resurrected.﴾ Za'm (claim) is saying something on the basis of conjecture, and it is also used for a lie.

Shurayh said: "Every thing has a kunya (euphemistic designation), and the kunya for a lie is 'they claim' (za'amu)." The phrase ﴿that they will never be resurrected﴾ stands in place of the object of za'ama. The "an" here is the lightened form of the heavy (an, mukhaffafa min al-thaqila), not the verbal-noun "an" (masdariyya), so that a governing particle does not enter upon another governing particle. The disbelievers meant are the disbelievers of the Arabs, and the meaning is: the disbelievers of the Arabs claimed that the matter is that they will never be resurrected, ever.

Then Allah, glorified is He, commanded His Messenger ﷺ to respond to them and refute their claim, so He said: ﴿Say: Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected, then you will surely be informed of what you did.﴾ Bala (yes/indeed) is the particle used to affirm a negation, so the meaning is: "Indeed, you will be resurrected."

Then He swore an oath to this, and the answer to the oath is "you will surely be resurrected", that is, you will surely come out of your graves. ﴿You will surely be informed of what you did﴾, that is, you will surely be told of it, as an establishment of proof against you, and then you will be recompensed for it. That resurrection and recompense ﴿is easy for Allah﴾, since restoration is easier than initial creation.

﴿So believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾: the fa' here is the explanatory fa' (al-fa' al-fasiha), indicating a hidden condition, meaning: if the matter is as such, then affirm Allah and His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, ﴿and the light which We have sent down﴾, which is the Qur'an, because it is a light by which one is guided out of the darkness of misguidance. ﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾: nothing of your statements and actions is hidden from Him, so He will recompense you for that.

﴿The Day He gathers you for the Day of Gathering﴾: the operator of the time expression is "you will surely be informed" (latunabba'unna), as stated by al-Nahhas.

Others said: its operator is "Acquainted" (khabir). It was also said: its operator is an omitted verb, which is "remember" (udhkur).

Abu al-Baqa' said: its operator is what the speech indicates, that is, "you will be mutually deceived on the Day He gathers you."

The majority read yajma'ukum with a fatha on the ya' and a damma on the 'ayn. It is narrated from Abu 'Amr that he read it with a sukun on the 'ayn, and there is no justification for this except lightening, even though this is not the place for it, as was read in ﴿wa ma yush'irukum﴾ [al-An'am: 109] with a sukun on the ra', and like the saying of the poet:

"So today I will drink, not bearing a sin from Allah, nor a fool's blame"

with a sukun on the ba' of "ashrab". Zayd ibn 'Ali, al-Sha'bi, Ya'qub, Nasr, Ibn Abi Ishaq, and al-Jahdari read najma'ukum with the nun. The meaning of ﴿for the Day of Gathering﴾ is the Day of Resurrection, for on it the people of the assembly are gathered for recompense, and on it every doer is gathered with his deed, every prophet with his community, and every wronged person with his wrongdoer.

﴿That is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain﴾: meaning that the Day of Resurrection is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain, because on it some of the people of the assembly defraud others. The people of truth defraud the people of falsehood, the people of faith defraud the people of disbelief, and the people of obedience defraud the people of disobedience. There is no greater defrauding than the people of Paradise defrauding the people of the Fire, when these enter Paradise and those enter the Fire, and they occupy their places which they would have occupied had they not done what necessitates the Fire. It is as if the people of the Fire have exchanged good for evil, the excellent for the inferior, and bliss for punishment, while the people of Paradise are the reverse of that.

It is said: "I defrauded so-and-so," when I traded with him or bought from him and the loss fell upon him and the advantage was mine; so said the exegetes. The one defrauded (maghbun) is the one who is defrauded of his people and his places in Paradise.

﴿And whoever believes in Allah and does righteous deeds—He will remove from him his misdeeds﴾: that is, whoever has affirmed with righteous action deserves the expiation of his misdeeds. The majority read yukaffir and yudkhilhu with the ya' (third person), while Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read both with the nun. The accusative of ﴿abidan khalidina fiha﴾ is as a predicated circumstantial state (hal muqaddara). The indicator "that" (dhalika) refers to what was mentioned of expiation and admission, and it is the subject, and its predicate is ﴿the great triumph﴾, that is, the victory that nothing equals.

﴿And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs—those are the companions of the Fire, abiding therein. And wretched is the destination﴾: the signs (ayat) here mean either the revealed verses or what is more general than them. Here Allah, glorified is He, mentioned the state of the blessed and the state of the wretched to explain the defrauding previously mentioned, and that it will occur because of the expiation and admission to Paradise for the first group, and because of the admission of the second group into the Fire and their abiding therein.

﴿No disaster strikes except by permission of Allah﴾: that is, no disaster among the calamities strikes anyone except by the permission of Allah, that is, by His decree and His measure. Al-Farra' said: "except by the permission of Allah" means by the command of Allah. It was also said: except by the knowledge of Allah.

It was said: the occasion of its revelation was that the disbelievers said: "If what the Muslims are upon were true, Allah would have protected them from calamities in this world."

Malik ibn Dinar, 'Amr ibn Dinar, and 'Ikrimah read "yahda'" with a sukun hamza and "qalbuhu" in the nominative, meaning: his heart becomes tranquil and calm. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of all things﴾: that is, of perfect knowledge, from which nothing is hidden.

﴿And obey Allah and obey the Messenger﴾: that is, make the calamities easy for yourselves, and occupy yourselves with obedience to Allah and obedience to His Messenger. ﴿But if you turn away﴾: that is, you turn away from obedience, ﴿then upon Our Messenger is only the clear notification﴾: he has no obligation beyond that, and he has done it. Then he directed to tawhid and reliance, saying: ﴿Allah—there is no deity but Him﴾: that is, He alone deserves worship to the exclusion of others, so affirm His unity and do not associate anything with Him. ﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾: that is, they should entrust their affairs to Him and depend upon Him, not upon anyone else.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, al-Bayhaqi, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Mas'ud that it was said to him: "Did you hear the Prophet ﷺ say anything about 'za'amu'?" He said: "I heard him say: 'It is the worst mount of a man.'"

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn 'Abbas who said: "The Day of Mutual Loss and Gain is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection."

'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him regarding ﴿That is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain﴾ that he said: "The people of Paradise defrauded the people of the Fire."

Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated from Ibn Mas'ud regarding ﴿No disaster strikes﴾ that he said: "They are the calamities which strike a man, and he knows that they are from Allah, so he submits to them and is content."

The plural pronoun was permissible in the first interpretation because the word ʿaduww (enemy) is used for the singular, the dual and the plural.

Then God, glorified is He, informed that wealth and children are a trial, saying: ﴿Indeed, your wealth and your children are only a trial﴾, that is, a test, an examination and a tribulation, which drive you to earn the forbidden and withhold the right of God. Then He, glorified is He, commanded them to piety and obedience, saying: ﴿So fear God as much as you are able﴾, that is, as much as you are capable of and your effort reaches.

The meaning of ﴿And listen and obey﴾ is: listen to what you are commanded, and obey the commands.

Abu ʿUbaydah said: it is the predicate (khabar) of the implied kāna (i.e., "let the spending be good for you").

The Kufans said: it is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (ḥāl). It was also said: it is the direct object (mafʿūl bihi) of "spend", meaning: so spend what is good.

The interpretation of this verse has already been given earlier.

Alas, time!" and I am Time.'" Then Abu Hurayrah recited: ﴿If you lend to God a goodly loan, He will multiply it for you﴾.

His saying: ﴿O you who believe, indeed among your spouses and your children there are enemies for you﴾. He means that they oppose you and distract you from good. The occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul) falls within this meaning by priority. It is that some men from Makkah accepted Islam and wanted to emigrate, but their spouses and children did not leave them. So God, glorified is He, commanded them to beware of them, and not to obey them in anything they wanted from them that opposed what God wills. The pronoun in ﴿so beware of them﴾ refers either to the enemy, or to the spouses and children, but not in a general sense; rather to those among them who are characterized by enmity. The plural pronoun was permissible in the first interpretation because the word ʿaduww (enemy) is used for the singular, the dual and the plural.

Then God guided them to pardon, saying: ﴿But if you pardon and overlook and forgive﴾, that is, pardon their sins that they committed, leave off reproaching them for them, and conceal them. ﴿Then indeed God is Forgiving, Merciful﴾, extending forgiveness and mercy to you and to them. It was said: the man whom his spouses and children held back from emigration, when he saw that people had preceded him to it and gained understanding of the religion, resolved to punish his spouses and children. So God revealed ﴿But if you pardon﴾, to the end of the verse. The verse is general in application, even if the occasion of revelation is specific, as we have explained to you more than once.

Mujahid said: "By God, they did not act as enemies to them in this world, but their affection for them led them to take the forbidden for them, so they gave it to them."

Then God, glorified is He, informed that wealth and children are a trial, saying: ﴿Indeed, your wealth and your children are only a trial﴾, that is, a test, an examination and a tribulation, which drive you to earn the forbidden and withhold the right of God. So do not obey them in disobedience to God. ﴿And God has with Him a great reward﴾ for whoever prefers the obedience of God and abandoning His disobedience over the love of his wealth and his child.

Then He, glorified is He, commanded them to piety and obedience, saying: ﴿So fear God as much as you are able﴾, that is, as much as you are capable of and your effort reaches.

A group of the people of knowledge held that this verse abrogates (nāsikhah, i.e. it is a case of naskh, abrogation) His saying: ﴿Fear God with the fear due to Him﴾ [Al ʿImran: 102]. Among them were Qatadah, al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas, al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd. We have explained the discussion of His saying ﴿Fear God with the fear due to Him﴾ [Al ʿImran: 102]. The meaning of ﴿And listen and obey﴾ is: listen to what you are commanded, and obey the commands.
